guitar.guitaristsText: John Lennon / George Harrison / Paul McCartney
guitar.modelsText: Rickenbacker 325/360-12, Gretsch, Epiphone Casino, Gibson J-160E
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: well documented across multiple guitars and eras — Lennon's Rickenbacker 325/Casino, Harrison's Gretsch/Rickenbacker 360-12, McCartney mainly bass (Hofner) with some guitar use.
guitar.notes: Original entry reasonable as a summary across three members and many guitars; kept as-is.

tone.target: bright Beatles rock rhythm with clean-to-edge crunch
tone.profile: bright Beatles rock rhythm with clean-to-edge crunch
tone.summary: A classic British rhythm tone using the UK 45 or US Deluxe amp model, boosted by Comp and colored by OD 9, finished with bright room ambience and Spring reverb to capture the Beatles' chimey sound.

rig.name: The Beatles - I Saw Her Standing There - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray hum and noise inherent in vintage rock tones.
Provide tight rhythm attack and smooth out dynamics for consistent strumming.
Add slight, breakup-style grit and warmth without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The OD 9 is used for light edge crunch rather than full overdrive.

blocks.purpose: Bypass. We want clean-to-edge breakup, not heavy distortion.
Simulate the bright, chimey sound of a classic British combo amp.
Provide a classic British cabinet voicing that complements the UK 45 amp model.
Boost the upper mids and treble frequencies to achieve a bright, jangly sound.
Bypass. No wah needed for this rhythm tone.
Bypass. Explicitly avoiding chorus as per the musical verdict.
Add subtle rhythmic depth without distracting from the main rhythm.
blocks.gap: A very light delay is used to enhance the 'jangly' feel.

blocks.purpose: Provide a small room ambience to give the sound space without sounding overly wet.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the chimey, jangly sound required for The Beatles' rhythm tone.

proposals.reason: The current IR is too generic; a specific vintage UK cab will enhance the jangly, chimey sound.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in upper mids/treble.
